newsitem.title: USA: Murkowski meets W. House's Bowles on nuclear waste.
newsitem.headline: Murkowski meets W. House's Bowles on nuclear waste.

text.p: Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski Tuesday met with White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles to urge the administration to support his nuclear waste interim storage bill.
"This was an opportunity for the chairman to make the Senate's case to the new chief of staff and he was thankful for that opportunity," an aide to the Alaska Republican said.
"The chairman told Mr. Bowles that the just-leave-it there policy was not good for the 41 states that are left with the waste," the aide said.

The Senate last year passed a bill to establish an interim storage facility in Nevada for waste accumulating at commercial nuclear reactors across the country. But President Clinton threatened to veto the measure and the House did not act on a companion bill.
Murkowski's aide said the senator is to meet with Bowles again on the issue.

The aide also said to his knowledge Bowles did not bring up the pending nomination of Federico Pena for energy secretary, after Murkowski this week again postponed a committee vote on the appointment.

White House officials have indicated they believe Murkowski is holding up Pena's nomination to try to get a deal from the White House on the nuclear waste issue, but Murkowski's aide said that is not the case.
"The issues are not directly linked, but the White House is holding up S-104 (nuclear storage bill)," the aide said.

Murkowski postponed a meeting scheduled for Wednesday because the committee still was checking some information on Pena and had not had time to complete the work since last week's congressional recess, the aide said.
He said another committee meeting to vote on the nomination has not yet been scheduled.

Associate Deputy Energy Secretary Kyle Simpson, speaking Tuesday with reporters, said, "Sen. Murkowski, the chairman, postponed the hearing yesterday. Conversations continue with the chairman, and we would hope that we could see a vote on Mr. Secretary Pena very soon."

Simpson, who had just come from a meeting with Saudi Arabian oil officials which Pena did not attend, said: "It would be nice to be able to move forward and have conversations on a number of issues that are important on a broad range of subjects with the secretary of the department."
